anchors.description: Michel's closed form satisfies dsigma_r/dr + (sigma_r-sigma_theta)/r + rho omega^2 r = 0 with the analytic derivative, normalised by (3+nu)/4 rho omega^2 b
d(r eps_theta)/dr - eps_r vanishes for the closed-form displacement, same normalisation
sigma_r at bore and rim, normalised by the bore hoop stress
the annular solution with a = 1e-4 b reproduces Michel's regular solid solution (stress and displacement) at r >= 0.2 b
a -> 0 limit: the bore hoop stress equals twice the centre stress of the solid disc

a/b -> 1 limit: sigma_theta collapses onto the thin-ring value rho omega^2 b^2. The approach is O(delta), not O(delta^2): at a = 0.999 b the residual is 1.7e-3, so the gate is 5e-3 and the measured slope is reported
t*int sigma_theta dr on the symmetry cut equals the exact centrifugal resultant of the sector (two independent derivations of the same equilibrium)
sum(forces_x) equals the exact centroid-triangulated integral of rho omega^2 x over the discretised polygonal domain (2x2 Gauss is exact for this integrand)
the same sum against the exact annular-sector resultant; the remainder is the chordal-area deficit of the inscribed polygon, O(dtheta^2), reported and not absorbed
sigma_theta at element centres vs exact: relative L2 and worst point (normalised by max|sigma_theta|) below 3 %

sigma_r at element centres vs exact; the worst point is normalised by the hoop scale because sigma_r vanishes at both surfaces, so its own L2 norm is an ill-scaled denominator (that raw figure is reported next to it)
nodal radial displacement vs exact: worst and L2 relative error below 3 %
the exact field has no tangential displacement; max|u_theta|/max|u_r| must stay at round-off
the exact field is shear-free in polar components; max|tau_rtheta|/max|sigma_theta|

bore hoop stress rebuilt from the element centres nearest the bore (the burst-driver quantity): three-point quadratic extrapolation, graded mesh, 1 % gate. The two-point linear value is reported next to it because that is what a post-processor does by default
x-reaction on the theta = pi/2 symmetry cut vs the analytic membrane force t*int sigma_theta dr -- equilibrium of the discrete model, not of the field
the sum of the x body forces equals the x reaction taken by the cut
observed orders of the hoop L2, radial L2 and displacement errors between the two finest rungs of the 6x6 / 12x12 / 24x24 ladder must be >= 1
radial grading towards the bore at equal degrees of freedom (12x24): the graded mesh must stay inside the gate and improve the bore value
bore hoop stress ratio sigma_theta(a)/(rho omega^2 b^2) recovered for a/b = 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.40 / 0.80 at 16x32 graded, each within 1 % of the closed form

three wrong models (20 % omega error, radius-free body force b = rho omega^2 e_r, plane strain instead of plane stress) must each break the 3 % gate, otherwise the field anchors above have no discriminating power

equal-split lumping of the centrifugal load is NOT detectable here: for a smooth load field both rules are O(h^2), so this anchor asserts that the lumped error stays inside the gate and records that a field comparison cannot find a load-rule bug of this kind
